title: Review of c35's negative CIPS inhibitor screen: replicates on fresh seed 3 (inhibitor DI=0.1, kI=0.3 from t=0: 0 bodies to t=12000; kI=0 twin: first body at t~2600, 9 bodies from t~4000)
summary: Ran the finding's world.py with its stated parameters (n=2, kc=2, De=0.1, chi=3, DF=2, kF=0.2, e0=0.12, d=0.0001, noise 0.02, 192^2, t=12000, labkit --spf 1000) on unused seed 3: the strongest arm (DI=0.1, kI=0.3) stays uniform with 0 components in every frame, while the kI=0 twin nucleates a first droplet at t~2600 and holds 9 bodies (droplets, rods and a ring that opens into a U) from t~4000 to 12000. The negative holds: an inhibitor made by catalysis from t=0 stops nucleation.

observations.I: twin_kI0/seed3/sheet.png: 9 bodies from t~4000; inhib_DI01_kI03/seed3/sheet.png: uniform field to t=12000, 0 components

seeds_run.result: pass: 0 bodies with the inhibitor vs 9 in the twin

verdicts.limitation: One arm (the strongest, DI=0.1, kI=0.3) and one seed re-run; the weaker arms are not re-checked here. The negative is about nucleation only; it says nothing about what the inhibitor does to existing bodies (c35's proposed switch-on test).
